jobs.title: Hazardous Waste Project Manager
jobs.description:
Clean Harbors is seeking a Technical Services Project Manager
will assist in growing the TS revenues and profitability in the business lines of Clean Pack, drum and bulk. The TS Project Manager will scope out, inventory, profile, secure approvals, draft and review safety plans, assess labor and equipment resources for opportunities that need more complex management and technical customer interaction. As required, the TS Project Manager will manage the team responsible for executing a project to assure it’s completed safely, on budget and exceeds the customer's expectations

Clean Harbors is the leading provider of environmental, energy and industrial services throughout the United States, Canada, Mexico and Puerto Rico. Everywhere industry meets environment, Clean Harbors is on-site, providing premier environmental, energy and industrial services. We are solving tough problems through innovation and proven methodology – come be part of the solution with us.

Why work for Clean Harbors?

Health and Safety is our #1 priority and we live it 3-6-5!
Focus on maintaining sustainability and cleaning the Earth
Recruiting Pay range: $75-$95K per /year
Comprehensive health benefits coverage after 30 days of full-time employment including 401K with Company match
Own part of the company with our Employee Stock Purchase Plan
Opportunities for growth and development for all the stages of your career
Company paid training and tuition reimbursement

Responsibilities

Ensures Health and Safety is the number one goal by following policies, processes, and acting in a safe manner at all time.
Prepare quotes or bids assure all costs are recognized and the quoted dollars meet required margins.
Prepare profiles both internal and external (third party) to manage the materials found in the scope of work. Secure appropriate approvals
Meets with customers to participate in job walks to understand the scope of work and any issues that may impact costs and execution.
Works with the Coordinators to schedule the work and assure availability of manpower and equipment resources.
Lead the team that executes the involved work and assure executed efficiently and safely
Follow up on jobs with operational team and customer to assure work completed satisfactorily, issues resolved, invoiced, and monies collected.
Perform other duties and tasks as assigned from time to time by management and will be required by the needs of the Clean Harbors business.

Qualifications

3+ years of experience
High School + specialized training or 1 year of college required.
Bachelor’s Degree with science major with chemistry classes preferred.
Alternative combinations of education and experience may be accepted in lieu of degree.
Past experience in Haz Waste management.
40 Hours OSHA and RCRA Training required.
Class B CDL w/Haz Waste Endorsement and Hi Haz Training preferred.
Leadership Skills to manage a team of chemists/technicians; computer skills; communication skills; confidence in dealing with new people and situations; Knowledge of the WIN System; Chemical Compatibilities; negotiating skills
communication skills; confidence in dealing with new people and situations; Knowledge of the WIN System
Negotiating Skills; Chemical compatibilities

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree
DOT knowledge and dispatching/ logistics experience
Leadership and supervisory knowledge
RCRA/OSHA knowledge

Clean Harbors Technical Services

Waste Disposal – Comprehensive disposal of hazardous and non-hazardous waste at Company-owned facilities
Recycling Services – Extensive recycling, reuse and reclamation options for materials such as solvents, chemicals, oil and electrical equipment
Chemical Packing – Safe, efficient handling and disposal of the widest range of chemicals, including reactives and compressed gases
Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) Services – HHW collection programs of all types and sizes, facilitated by Clean Harbors expert personnel

Clean Harbors is an equal opportunity employer.

Clean Harbors is committed to providing access, equal opportunity and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. To request reasonable accommodation, contact ect@cleanharbors.com or 1-844-922-5547.

Clean Harbors is a Military & Veteran friendly company.

Please be advised that Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools may be used to support certain stages of the recruitment process but are not used as a replacement for human decision making.

Clean Harbors is committed to complying with applicable pay transparency laws and ensuring fair and equitable compensation. The posted salary range reflects the minimum and maximum target for this role. Final compensation may vary based on factors such as location, experience, skills, and business needs. In addition to the base salary, some roles may be eligible for bonus or incentive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package.

jobs.title: Water Laboratory - Water Quality Analyst Level 2
jobs.location: Macquarie Park, New South Wales, Australia
jobs.description:
Join a supportive team with training, development, and growth opportunities

Full-time opportunity based in North Ryde

EA5 salary of $81,926.04 + super | 6-month temporary opportunity with potential for extension or permanency

About The Role 

Join a hands-on field and laboratory team responsible for collecting and analysing water, environmental, and operational samples that support Sydney Water’s services and regulatory obligations. Working across a variety of environments, you will use specialised equipment and established procedures to perform routine and non-routine sampling activities, ensuring high-quality, accurate, and timely results. With a strong focus on safety, compliance, and customer service, you will play an important role in delivering essential environmental and operational monitoring outcomes.

Responsibilities: 

Collect and analyse routine and non-routine environmental, water, wastewater, soil, and sediment samples in accordance with established procedures.
Operate, maintain, and calibrate field and laboratory equipment to ensure accurate and reliable results.
Review data for accuracy, identify anomalies, and promptly escalate issues or unusual results to supervisors.
Support quality assurance activities, including audits, documentation reviews, instrument checks, and compliance with accredited systems.
Work collaboratively with team members to meet customer, regulatory, operational, and service delivery requirements.
Maintain a strong commitment to safety, continuous improvement, and learning while working across different locations, rosters, and operational environments as required.

About You 

Relevant Science qualification or experience in a field or laboratory-based scientific role.
Experience collecting, processing, or analysing environmental, water, wastewater, or biological samples.
Demonstrated ability to operate scientific equipment and laboratory information systems (LIMS).
Strong attention to detail with experience maintaining accurate data, records, and quality standards.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced operational environment.
Current Driver's Licence and willingness to work across field and laboratory settings as required.

This recruitment will be used to create a talent pool for current and future opportunities within Sydney Water. 

Please note as part of the application process, you will be asked to undergo background checks which includes a criminal history check and a medical assessment either online or in person. 

Applications close Tuesday 1st December at 11.59 AEST 

We support you throughout the application process and can provide adjustments where required. For more information, please contact Ranya Kumar, Talent Acquisition Partner at
ranya.kumar@sydneywater.com.au 

Please refer to the JOB PROFILE for full role accountabilities. 

Dive into Our Great Benefits:  

Competitive Remuneration:
 We’ll ensure that your skills and contributions are valued and rewarded appropriately.  
Hybrid Work Environment: 
We offer a hybrid work model that balances remote work and office collaboration, supporting our team's productivity and well-being.  
Continuous Professional Growth: 
We will invest in your career with leadership and development programs to propel your success.  
24/7 Wellbeing Support:
 Access for you and your family to free and confidential mental health and general health support through our EAP portal.  
Discounted Private Health Insurance: 
Unlock affordable access to top-tier health coverage with our discounted insurance plans.  
Family First:
 Prioritise your family with up to 18 weeks of fully paid parental leave and a childcare allowance.  
Fitness Passport: 
Achieve your physical fitness goals using our Fitness Passport, granting you access to a multitude of gyms and pools across NSW.  
Novated Leasing:
 Get in the driver's seat of your financial future with our novated lease options.  

As part of the application process, Sydney Water will be collecting your personal information to assess your suitability for the role. Your personal information may also be used to establish a Dayforce talent profile. Your personal information will be collected in accordance with Dayforce’s Terms and Privacy Policy and Sydney Water’s Privacy Collection Statement – recruitment. Please note as part of the application process, you will be asked to undergo background checks which include a criminal history check.

jobs.title: Environmental Health Officer
jobs.description:
Professional expertise. Personal purpose.

As an Environmental Health Officer, you help protect public health and improve local environmental outcomes across Blacktown City. You inspect food premises, cooling towers, commercial swimming pools and on-site sewerage systems, investigate pollution complaints, and respond to public health incidents. You provide advice to businesses, residents and other stakeholders, helping keep local places and spaces clean, healthy and safe.

You develop and implement environmental health projects, policies, guidelines and programs that support Council’s environmental sustainability commitments. You assess environmental health issues, prepare reports and correspondence, deliver presentations, and contribute to community education initiatives that encourage practical action on environmental and public health matters.

Your work has a direct impact on everyday life. It helps manage environmental and public health risks, supports compliance with legislation, and contributes to a healthier, more sustainable city for our community.

You communicate clearly, write high-quality reports and correspondence, solve problems using sound judgement, and use Microsoft Office and corporate systems confidently.

At Blacktown City Council, Good People Make Great Teams, And Great Teams Build Great Cities. Here, You Will Find The Stability And Support To Keep Growing, Along With

a secure, permanent, full-time role with one of Australia's largest councils
an entry level salary commencing at $1,866.69 per week
a 35-hour working week
a car allowance
access to Council's flextime arrangement
12% superannuation and competitive leave entitlements
ongoing training and development support
access to Fitness Passport, social clubs and wellbeing programs.

Our commitment to safety

Blacktown City Council is committed to safety. We have introduced alcohol and other drug testing at the pre-employment phase, and via a series of random and cause testing.

We are a child safe organisation that supports and promotes the safety, wellbeing and empowerment of children.

Position Description

to view or download the position description.

Closing date: Sunday 6 December 2026, 11.59 pm

Contact officer: Julia Lindon on 9839 6295

Internal ref: BCC1686
